mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20d returns in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60d returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60d returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo MA AND RSAFS > 12-mo MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for four consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60d returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods.
